name: rea
description: Reverse engineer anything with agents, from app behavior down to native binaries.
one_liner: An AI helper that pries open other people's apps and files to show you exactly how they work under the hood, down to the raw machine code.
buyer: A security consultant or competitive-intelligence analyst who gets paid to figure out how a rival's app, device, or file format actually works, without source code.
business_use_cases: A security audit firm uses it to quickly map how a client's legacy desktop app or firmware actually behaves before writing a penetration-test report.
A competitive-intelligence analyst at a hardware startup uses it to understand how a competitor's companion app talks to its device, to spot a feature gap to build against.
A digital-forensics investigator uses it to reconstruct what an unknown binary found on a compromised machine actually does, for an incident report.

money_ideas.idea: Offer paid reverse-engineering-as-a-service engagements for clients who need a one-off binary or app analyzed but don't want to run the tooling themselves.
Sell a hosted, higher-limit version with saved analysis history for security teams doing this regularly.

steal_this: Package it as a weekend side-gig: offer fixed-price 'tell me how this app/binary works' reports on freelance platforms, aimed at other developers who need to interoperate with an undocumented system.
